title: Seymour’s second-neighborhood conjecture
formal: Does every finite nonempty oriented graph D contain a vertex v for which |\(N^{++}(v)|\ge |N^{+}(v)|\), where \(N^{+}(v)\) consists of vertices at directed distance one from v and \(N^{++}(v)\) consists of vertices at directed distance exactly two?
definitions: An oriented graph is a finite vertex set V and an arc set \(A\subseteq V\times V\) with no loops and with at most one of \((u,v),(v,u)\) present for each distinct pair. Arc multiplicities are not allowed. \(N^{+}(v)=\{u:(v,u)\in A\}\). \(N^{++}(v)\)={\(w\in V\setminus (N^{+}(v)\cup \{v\})\): there exists u with \((v,u)\in A\) and \((u,w)\in A\)}. Thus a vertex already in the first neighborhood is not counted in the second, even if it is also reachable by a length-two walk. Cardinalities count vertices rather than paths or arcs. A sink has both sets empty and satisfies the inequality. No lower bound on outdegree, connectivity or planarity is imposed.
answer_criterion: Prove the proposition in the problem statement or its logical negation with the stated model, hypotheses and quantifier order. The proof must settle the entire target. A result conditional on an additional assumption settles only that conditional version. Benchmark acceptance requires a complete proof checked by a proof assistant and matching this statement.
why: Ask whether every oriented graph has a vertex whose new two-step reach is at least its immediate reach.

importance.reason: Seymour’s second-neighborhood conjecture is a classical universal expansion principle for arbitrary oriented graphs, with broad extremal significance.

progress.text: Glover’s revised manuscript claims a complete proof. This review has not verified that claim or established community acceptance.
Bai, Li and Park still explicitly state the general conjecture as open and prove special cases of a stronger matching property.

context_blocks.text: The first out-neighborhood measures one-step reach. The second counts genuinely new vertices obtainable in two steps. The conjecture asserts that at least one starting point has no decrease in this particular count.

Excluding opposite arcs matters: a two-vertex directed 2-cycle would have a nonempty first neighborhood and an empty second neighborhood at both vertices. The oriented-graph hypothesis rules out this immediate obstruction.

The July 2026 specialist paper retains the general conjecture while treating a strengthening. A separate May 2026 manuscript claims a full solution. This conflict is recorded explicitly; the card does not certify a proof or dismiss the claim without analysis.

sentences: Seymour’s conjecture concerns oriented graphs with no loops or opposite pair of arcs.
It asks for a vertex with at least as many vertices at distance exactly two as at distance one.
Second neighbors exclude first neighbors and count vertices rather than paths.
The statement is a general local expansion principle without degree or planarity promises.
A complete-proof claim conflicts with a later specialist paper still treating the conjecture as open, and that status uncertainty is preserved.
